newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine trade unions call Dec 26 walkout.
newsitem.headline: Argentine trade unions call Dec 26 walkout.

text.p: Argentina's trade unions on Friday called a 24-hour strike for Dec. 26 to protest against presidential decrees on labour reforms.
CGT union federation chief Rodolfo Daer told reporters after a three-hour meeting of CGT delegates that workers would stay home next Thursday, but would not stage any public protests.
Daer said the CGT would also challenge the labour decrees in court and would meet again on Dec. 30 to debate a long-term battle plan.
Late on Wednesday President Carlos Menem ended weeks of negotiations with the unions and bypassed reluctant lawmakers by introducing the country's first labour reforms by decree.
The decrees erode the trade union monopoly on health insurance plans and reduce their wage bargaining power.
Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said on Thursday all but one of the pending reforms would be introduced by decree, the exception being a new severance payment system.
The unions last went on strike in September against Menem's economic policy.
